signature: A bright, silent, seemingly endless modern library that feels like the way out: in its centre metal letters say 'the end is near' over terminals that buzz far too loudly, every straight walk loops back to them and leaves a wall behind you, the floor drops you between other shelves, and somewhere close by a home and an evening field you almost remember fray into the stacks, with six people around a cold fire and a door that only sometimes goes anywhere.

exits.source_quote: The fake realities of The End can sometimes contain exits into other, safer Levels. However, this is not consistent.
exits.adaptation_reason: The page says only that fake realities sometimes contain exits and that this is not consistent. Which doors, and the odds, are ours: the home's front door (28% per try) and the field's gate (14% per try), rolled fresh on every try, so the same door works and fails. A failed try breaches the border: you are in the stacks again and everything is normal (page: breaching a border returns everything to normal). The destination is unnamed, so 'to' is the placeholder EXT and the route reports as not built.
exits.conditions: inside a fake reality; per-try chance, never consistent; most tries breach back into the library
exits.hint: The house's front door glows with an evening you have not seen in a long time. Doors here are not to be trusted.

entity_policy: No entity is spawned. Partygoers (REPORTED) exist only as the page's warning: a note at the terminals, rising buzz and smiling screens after use, and the off-screen 'taken' fail state; the 'host' they refer to is mentioned once, unnamed, in that note. No other wanderer is ever shown in the library (SOURCE: wanderers cannot perceive each other). Inside the field fake reality the six Junkies are perceivable humans (SOURCE: humans are perceived normally there): static, slumped around a cold fire, non-hostile, unwilling to trade without Memory Juice; nothing is traded because the page does not say what they offer. The page's closing first-person 'smile' monologue is TESTIMONY from an unnamed, unreliable narrator: it appears only as a paraphrased, explicitly labelled terminal message and as the '=)' sign-off on the screens; none of its claims (sending messages, altering articles, named persons) is treated as fact.
notes: SOURCE (rev 119; banner says the page is being rewritten): a supposed trap level that creates the illusion of escaping; a seemingly endless modern library; a central main area decorated with metal letters spelling 'the end is near'; near-complete silence (some areas at -6.2 dB); the centre almost as silent but its computer terminals buzz loudly; advice to stay in the centre to avoid isolation; unstable geometry: walking one way loops and turning around then meets a wall; frequent random no-clipping that does not exit; wanderers unable to perceive other wanderers; fake realities: personalised sub-areas replicating familiar environments, physical, with humans perceivable normally, close together, blending transitionally, and returning everything to normal when a border is breached; all electricity fails until you leave except the terminals, which connect to any Wi-Fi; terminals advised against (Partygoers and possibly their 'host'; three reports of abductions); the Junkies (six people, an outpost in the fake realities, trade only with Memory Juice, intoxicate to feel at home, B.N.T.G. rescues failed); entrances: doors that would indicate an exit, most commonly with a neon sign above, or rarely a no-clip fall; exits sometimes inside fake realities, not consistent, no reliable way out. TESTIMONY: the unattributed first-person monologue at the end of the exits section. ADAPTATION: (1) the page gives no map. The playable world is a finite streaming window (ChunkWorld, 24 m chunks, radius 2) over a plan that repeats exactly every 6 chunks (a 144 m period cell): the main area, the two fake realities and the stack layouts recur, so walking one way brings you back to the letters. Crossing a period seam arms a wall across the aisle behind you, placed the moment the seam is out of view; it follows you along the seam and moves to the next seam you cross. (2) Library grammar: 2.1 m double-sided shelf runs (birch end panels, white steel, seeded book spines) in 8.8 m segments on a 2.2 m pitch with 12 m column grid, seeded orientation per chunk; some chunks hold reading tables or a sunken reading pit (three 0.18 m risers). Ceiling 3.2 m. (3) Light: because 'anything that uses electricity' fails, the library is lit by frosted skylights and clerestory ribbons (daylight, never seen directly); desk lamps and downlights are dead. The only screens that glow are the terminals. (4) Main area: a 20.8 m double-height hall (roof 7.6 m) with a 12 m void under one big frosted skylight, a gallery ring at 3.6 m reached by a 20-riser stair, glass balustrades, shelves on the gallery, reading tables beneath; letters on the north wall above the gallery, eight terminals on a back-to-back desk island in the void, buzzing (synth transformer hum). (5) Silence is a very low room tone; isolation (0-1) rises with distance from the nearest main area and eases there or in a fake reality: desaturation, vignette, thicker haze, the room tone drops further and your heartbeat comes up; random no-clips (every ~55-140 s outside the centre and fake realities, more often when isolated) drop you between other shelves 24-48 m away, never out of the level. (6) Fake realities: the page gives none in detail, so we built two personalised but generic ones side by side in every period cell: a family living room and kitchen at dusk whose floorboards, walls and ceiling fray into the stacks (a shelf run pushes into the room), with an open back door onto a garden that becomes an open field under a painted evening sky; the field holds a dead vending machine (from the page's 'corrupted' image credit, a field with a vending machine) and the Junkies' outpost. Walking toward them blends the light and haze gradually; leaving across a border snaps everything back to the library at once. (7) Terminals: first use connects (to any network) and shows an anonymous '=)'; every screen then shows it and the buzz rises; second use shows a labelled-testimony message; third use is the 'taken' fail state. (8) The flashlight is switched off the instant it comes on. (9) Arrival 'start' is the neon-sign-door entrance: you stand inside the hall in front of a plain door whose neon EXIT sign is dead on this side; it does not open. Arrival 'from_L085' (Level 85's documented library no-clip, edge L085>L601#2) drops you into an aisle west of the main area facing it. (10) Notes are paraphrases in our words (survey notes on a reading table, a warning taped to the terminal desk, a B.N.T.G. tag at the gate). Not built: L601>EXT#2 (undocumentable by the page), the B.N.T.G. themselves, Partygoer bodies, any trade, any measurement of the -6.2 dB areas (no instrument works here). QA FIXTURE: in QA mode only, the fake-reality door always opens (the walker bot walks from the hall to the home's front door and fires L601>EXT#1 through the normal interact logic) and random no-clips are off; qa_self_test exercises the inconsistent door, the seam wall, the no-clip, the blend/breach, the terminals and isolation.
